channel.title: Utica Midstream
channel.description: A free daily read on oil and gas from wellhead to market: prices, stocks, pipelines, policy, projects and people, with every fact sourced and dated.

item.title: US pushed Venezuela and Iraq to weigh leaving OPEC, Reuters reports, days before OPEC+ meets
item.description: Washington has been nudging two of OPEC's founders toward the door. Reuters, citing 10 people, reports the US encouraged Venezuela and Iraq this year to consider leaving the group and blocked Venezuela's dues.

item.title: Brent settles at $96.57 as Iran reports mine strikes and Ras Tanura loadings reportedly halt
item.description: What happens to US crude when the Gulf's export doors start closing? Brent settled up 2% at $96.57 on Thanksgiving after Iran's Guards said two tankers hit mines near Hormuz and CNN reported Saudi loadings stopped at Ras Tanura.

item.title: Brent jumps 3.5% as the Houthis claim a strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery
item.description: Ras Tanura, Saudi Arabia's largest refinery, is a target again. The Houthis claimed a strike there on Wednesday, Saudi air defenses said they downed four drones, and Brent settled up 3.5% at $94.61.

item.title: Oil gives back Tuesday's gain as glut fears outweigh new ship attacks near Hormuz
item.description: Shipping attacks near Hormuz are moving oil for a day at a time. Brent jumped more than 2% on Tuesday after three vessels were hit, then gave back $1.35 by early Wednesday as surplus worries for 2027 returned.

item.title: Oil falls to a three month low as the Iran war premium fades and stocks of crude build
item.description: $79.57. That was WTI early Tuesday, the lowest since late August, after crude lost 4.5% on Monday as Washington signaled more time for Iran diplomacy and inventory data pointed to a surplus.

item.title: A tanker incident at the US blockade line tests oil's calm as Iran stages tankers at Kharg
item.description: Is Iran testing the US blockade? UKMTO reported a tanker incident involving military forces in the Gulf of Oman on Sunday, and Iranian media claimed two tankers hit mines east of Hormuz. Neither report is confirmed, and oil futures barely moved early Monday.

item.title: Ohio permits 2,150 MW of gas power for data centers as Rockies Express seeks bids for a new lateral
item.description: Two Ohio villages, 2,150 MW of new gas-fired power, all of it for data centers. On November 19 the state siting board permitted an 800 MW plant in Ashville and a 1,350 MW plant in Millersport.

item.title: Bakken producers truck crude to Dakota Access as Enbridge's North Dakota line stays curtailed
item.description: Bakken producers are trucking crude to Dakota Access while Enbridge's 475,000 b/d North Dakota Pipeline stays curtailed over organic chloride testing, and at least two Midwest refiners have declared force majeure.

item.title: FERC approves Cheniere's three train Sabine Pass expansion and two new feed pipelines
item.description: FERC approved Cheniere's three train Sabine Pass LNG expansion in Louisiana on Thursday, about 20 million tonnes a year of new capacity, plus the Creole Trail and Sabine Crossing feed pipelines.

item.title: Bakken crude backs up as Enbridge's North Dakota line stays down over contamination
item.description: Enbridge's 475,000 barrel a day North Dakota Pipeline has been delayed over crude quality testing, with reports of organic chlorides in Bakken crude and a force majeure at a Minnesota refinery.

item.title: Crude slips toward $84 as a supply glut outruns the Hormuz war premium
item.description: Oil is falling even with tankers still hitting mines in the Gulf. WTI traded near $84 and Brent near $92 this morning as record US output, rising inventories and higher Russian exports outweighed the Hormuz risk.
